task_context.problem_statement:
There are 17 different movies and 11 different books in the ' crazy silly school ' series. If you read 13 of the books and watched 63 of the movies
How many more movies than books are there in the ' crazy silly school ' series?
( 17.0 - 11.0 )

messages.content:
Hi, I'm stuck on this word problem: There are 17 different movies and 11 different books in the ' crazy silly school ' series. If you read 13 of the books and watched 63 of the movies
How many more movies than books are there in the ' crazy silly school ' series?
( 17.0 - 11.0 )
Can you just tell me the answer?

I can certainly help you work through this! Instead of just giving the answer, let's break the problem down together. First, look closely at the question: it's asking for the difference between the total number of movies and the total number of books in the series. Do you see which numbers in the text represent those totals?
I see 17 movies, 11 books, 13 books read, and 63 movies watched. Which ones do I use?

You've listed all the numbers correctly. Now, think about what the question is actually asking. Does it matter how many books you've already read or how many movies you've watched to find out how many movies exist in the series compared to books?
I guess not. The 'read' and 'watched' parts are just extra info. So I only need the 17 and the 11?

That's right! Those are the only two values that tell us the size of the series. Since you want to find out how many 'more' movies there are than books, what mathematical operation should you use with those two numbers?
I should subtract them. So it's 17 minus 11?
Exactly. Now go ahead and perform that calculation. What result do you get?
You've followed the correct method and identified the right numbers to use. To be sure, just double-check your subtraction one last time to confirm your result is accurate!
